requirements.title: Level-5 expressions are the logical-operator layers over level-4 expressions
requirements.definition: Level-5 expressions are level-4 expressions optionally involving .NOT., .AND., .OR., .EQV., and .NEQV. The grammar layers not before level-4, then and, then or, then equivalence.
requirements.oracle:
Future controls must use logical operands with literal truth tables and must not claim evaluation short-circuit behavior beyond later evaluation rules.

requirements.title: An and-operand is an optional .NOT. followed by a level-4 expression
requirements.definition: The and-operand syntax is an optional not-op followed by level-4-expr. A second unparenthesized not-op is not admitted by this rule because the operand after not-op is level-4, not another and-operand.

requirements.oracle:
Negative plans must carefully avoid valid parses such as (.NOT. a) .AND. b; only forms where the token after .NOT. cannot be level-4 are attributable to R1015.

requirements.title: An or-operand is a left-recursive chain of and-operands joined by .AND.
requirements.definition: The or-operand syntax is either an and-operand or an or-operand followed by and-op and and-operand, giving .AND. left-recursive grouping above .OR. and equivalence.
requirements.oracle:
Intrinsic .AND. controls use LOGICAL operands and literal truth values for admission and truth-table checks only; they cannot observe grouping. The grouping facet can be addressed only by a value-based non-associative defined extension on a derived type with independently computed component oracles and valid defined-operation interfaces under 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2. Type errors remain 10.1.5.4 dependencies, not R1016 syntax evidence.

requirements.title: A level-5 expression is a left-recursive chain of equiv-operands joined by .EQV. or .NEQV.
requirements.definition: The level-5-expr syntax is either an equiv-operand or a level-5-expr followed by equiv-op and equiv-operand, making equivalence operators the lowest intrinsic logical layer and left-recursive.
requirements.oracle:
Intrinsic LOGICAL controls can admit .EQV. and .NEQV. and check their truth tables, but they cannot close the left-recursive grouping facet because intrinsic .EQV./.NEQV. chains are value-associative in two-valued logic and 10.1.5.4.2 allows equivalent evaluation subject to parentheses. A future grouping oracle must use a non-associative defined extension on a derived type, independently computed component results for the two parenthesisations, and valid defined-operation interfaces under 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2; do not use side effects or operand evaluation paths.
